items.question: How often is the proxy list updated and tested?
items.answer: The proxy pool is re-validated continuously every 60 seconds by Hydra, a multi-threaded Rust validation engine. Nodes that fail TCP socket handshakes, TLS negotiation, or response deadlines are placed into cooldown or purged immediately, ensuring zero stale endpoints in the active pool.

items.question: Are these proxies free, and do they require API keys?
items.answer: All endpoints (JSON feed, plain-text files, and web directory) are 100% free and open-source under MIT / CC-BY 4.0 licenses. No sign-ups, subscriptions, or API keys are required. You can consume raw feeds directly via GitHub's global CDN with zero rate limits.

items.question: What is the difference between SOCKS5 and HTTP proxies for web scraping?
items.answer: HTTP proxies operate at the application layer and tunnel HTTP/HTTPS traffic via the CONNECT method. SOCKS5 operates at layer 5 (session layer), routing arbitrary TCP and UDP traffic without altering request headers. For tools like curl, Python httpx, and Puppeteer, SOCKS5 with remote DNS resolution (socks5h://) prevents DNS leaks and minimizes target-side bot detection.

items.question: How do you classify proxy anonymity (Elite vs Anonymous vs Transparent)?
items.answer: Anonymity is determined during Hydra's protocol inspection: Elite (Level 1) forwards no identifying proxy headers (Via, X-Forwarded-For), making requests indistinguishable from direct visits; Anonymous (Level 2) conceals your real IP but declares proxy presence; Transparent (Level 3) transmits your client IP in headers. We recommend Elite and Anonymous nodes for scraping.

items.question: How should I handle proxy rotation and prevent IP bans?
items.answer: Pull a local pool from our raw endpoints (data/proxies.json or working_proxies.txt). Filter nodes by RTT < 1000ms and uptime > 80%. Rotate your egress IP every 10–25 requests or immediately upon receiving HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) or 403 (Forbidden). Always apply jitter to request intervals and rotate User-Agent headers alongside IPs.

items.question: How can I integrate this proxy pool into Python, Node.js, or cURL?
items.answer: Fetch https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stormsia/proxy-list/main/data/proxies.json for rich metadata or socks5.txt for flat host:port pairs. In cURL, route via 'curl -x socks5h://host:port https://httpbin.org/ip'. In Python, pass the proxy URL to requests or httpx.AsyncClient(proxy='socks5://host:port'). Check our Docs & API page for complete, runnable code examples.

faqs.question: What are datacenter proxies and what are their technical advantages?
faqs.answer: Datacenter proxies originate from cloud hosting providers and commercial server facilities (AWS, Hetzner, OVH, DigitalOcean). They provide Gigabit uplink bandwidth, minimal packet jitter, and predictable sub-second round-trip latency (often RTT < 400ms).

faqs.question: What workloads are datacenter proxies best suited for?
faqs.answer: They are ideal for high-throughput web scraping, API stress testing, price monitoring, streaming data ingestion, and bulk asset downloads where network speed and bandwidth take priority over residential ASN stealth.

faqs.question: How frequently are datacenter nodes monitored?
faqs.answer: Hydra's multi-threaded Rust engine audits every datacenter IP every 60 seconds. Sockets failing connection deadlines or dropping TLS handshakes are pruned immediately.

faqs.question: What are residential proxies and how do they differ from datacenter IPs?
faqs.answer: Residential proxies route traffic through IP addresses assigned by consumer Internet Service Providers (such as Comcast, AT&T, Vodafone, or Deutsche Telekom) to residential households. Because target websites see organic residential ASN ranges, these requests encounter significantly lower CAPTCHA rates and WAF blocks compared to datacenter IPs.

faqs.question: Why is the pool of free residential proxies smaller than datacenter lists?
faqs.answer: Consumer broadband connections are dynamic and subject to frequent disconnects and IP reassignments. As a result, public residential nodes have higher churn. Hydra audits these nodes every 60 seconds to prune offline endpoints immediately.

faqs.question: How should I structure scrapers using public residential proxies?
faqs.answer: Implement conservative request timeouts (5–8 seconds), handle connection retries with exponential backoff, and combine residential IPs with header randomization to preserve session hygiene.

about.socks5: SOCKS5 operates at OSI Layer 5 (Session Layer), routing arbitrary TCP and UDP packets without inspecting or modifying application payload headers. By configuring remote DNS resolution via socks5h://, your scraper prevents local DNS leak traces and bypasses domain-level SNI filtering. SOCKS5 is the recommended standard for Python httpx, Puppeteer, Playwright, and high-concurrency data scraping pipelines.
about.socks4: SOCKS4 is an established stream-oriented proxy protocol designed strictly for TCP connections (IPv4 only, no UDP support and no native user authentication). It introduces minimal transport overhead, making it useful for legacy automation tools, socket wrappers, and network testing where basic IP relaying is sufficient.
about.http: HTTP proxies operate at OSI Layer 7 (Application Layer), handling direct HTTP GET/POST requests and relaying them to destination web servers. When evaluated as Elite or Anonymous, they strip identifying headers. They integrate natively with standard command-line tools like cURL, Wget, and default HTTP clients across Node.js, Go, and Python.
about.https: HTTPS proxies support the HTTP CONNECT tunneling method (RFC 2817), establishing an opaque end-to-end TCP tunnel between your client and the target server. Because TLS encryption is negotiated directly between your client and the destination, the proxy server only sees raw encrypted ciphertext and destination hostnames, ensuring end-to-end confidentiality.

protocol.faqQ1: How do I connect to a {protocol} proxy using cURL or Python?
protocol.faqA1Socks5: In cURL, run: `curl -x socks5h://host:port https://httpbin.org/ip`. The socks5h protocol ensures DNS resolution occurs on the proxy server. In Python, install `httpx socksio` and initialize: `client = httpx.AsyncClient(proxy='socks5://host:port')`.
protocol.faqA1Other: In cURL, pass the proxy flag: `curl -x {protocol}://host:port https://httpbin.org/ip`. In Python requests: `requests.get('https://example.com', proxies={'http': '{protocol}://host:port', 'https': '{protocol}://host:port'})`.
protocol.faqA2: Every node in the {protocol} pool is audited every 60 seconds by our multi-threaded Hydra Rust validator. Dead nodes, high packet-loss servers, and unresponsive sockets are culled immediately.
protocol.faqQ3: Can I use these {protocol} proxies for high-volume web scraping?
protocol.faqA3: Yes. For best results, pool multiple nodes from data/proxies.json, filter for latency under 1000ms and uptime above 80%, and rotate exit nodes on each request cycle or upon hitting HTTP 429/403 status codes.

about.missionP1: Traditional free proxy lists suffer from extreme data staleness: 80% to 95% of listed IPs are offline, unresponsive, or blacklisted. The mission of stormsia/proxy-list is to provide developers, data scientists, and autonomous AI agents with an auditable, high-availability public proxy pool filtered every 60 seconds.
about.missionP2: We believe in an open web. Our infrastructure operates with zero authentication, no paywalls, no tracking redirects, and no collection of private user credentials.
about.hydraIntro: The backbone of our dataset reliability is Hydra, an open-source Rust engine built on asynchronous Tokio non-blocking sockets. Hydra inspects tens of thousands of candidate endpoints simultaneously:

privacy.description: Privacy Policy for stormsia/proxy-list: zero-log commitments, no personal data collection, and public proxy security recommendations.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.subtitle: Transparency, zero-log commitments, and public proxy security disclosures.
privacy.sec1P1: stormsia/proxy-list is built with a zero-collection architecture. We do not require account registration, do not request email addresses or personal identities, do not issue mandatory API keys, and never collect billing details.
privacy.sec1P2: We do not deploy third-party advertising pixels, behavioral trackers, or retargeting beacons. All web pages and data assets are distributed via GitHub and Fastly CDN edges.
privacy.sec2P1: All proxy endpoints published in proxies.json and plain text feeds are publicly reachable nodes aggregated from open upstream sources and verified by Hydra. stormsia/proxy-list does not own, operate, or host these proxy servers.
privacy.sec2P2: Hydra telemetry contains strictly technical operational metrics: TCP/TLS handshake latency, ISO country codes, Autonomous System Numbers (ASN), and header anonymity flags. No client traffic is ever routed through our infrastructure.
privacy.sec3P1: Public proxies are operated by independent third parties across various networks. Therefore:
privacy.sec3EncDesc: Never transmit unencrypted credentials or sensitive payloads over plain HTTP proxies. Always enforce HTTPS or authenticated TLS.
privacy.sec3DnsDesc: Use remote DNS resolution (socks5h://) to ensure domain queries are resolved at the proxy node rather than leaking through your local ISP.
